statement: Whenever `preorder_traversal(root)` returns `Ok(r)`, the vector r is exactly the preorder traversal of root. Define P(Tree.Null) = [] and P(Tree.Node(v,L,R)) = [v] concatenated with P(L) concatenated with P(R). Then len(r) = n and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] is the i-th element (0-indexed) of P(root). Equivalently, the values are visited in the order: root (if present), then the entire preorder traversal of the left subtree, then the entire preorder traversal of the right subtree.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree. Let n be the number of Tree.Node constructors in root. The problem constraints hold: 0 <= n <= 100, and every node value v stored in root satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

statement: The call `preorder_traversal(root)` returns `Ok(r)` for some vector r of 64-bit integers; it never returns `Err`.

statement: Whenever `preorder_traversal(root)` returns `Ok(r)`, for every 64-bit integer x, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = x equals the number of nodes in root whose stored value is x.
